title: Kestrel Closed-End Consumer Lease Credit Policy: Relationship Exposure
content:
**Relationship exposure limit — Kestrel Closed-End Consumer Lease**

**Clause.** Relationship exposure is the adjusted lease balance of every lease of the customer in active or maturity-extended status, plus the principal balance on every open Kestrel New Vehicle Retail, Kestrel Pre-Owned Retail and Kestrel Advantage Balloon contract of the customer, plus the adjusted capitalized cost of the lease being booked. Relationship exposure must not exceed the relationship exposure cap of the lease tier being booked. When it would, the lease is not funded and no partial approval is given.

**When the limit is tested**: at booking and at funding of a new lease.

**Evidence**: the figures come from the company's records of the customer's accounts — the lease balances, the contract principal balances and the adjusted capitalized cost on the lease being booked — matched to the customer by customer reference. A customer's own statement of a balance does not replace the record.

**Components at a glance**

| Component | Included | Not included |
|---|---|---|
| Customer's other leases | adjusted lease balance of leases in active or maturity-extended status | leases in any other status |
| Customer's retail, pre-owned and balloon contracts | principal balance of every open contract | contracts that are not open |
| The lease being booked | its adjusted capitalized cost | — |

**Worked illustration (all figures hypothetical)**

A customer has one active lease with an adjusted lease balance of $18000, one open retail contract with a principal balance of $12000, and a returned lease awaiting its lease-end bill. The new lease has an adjusted capitalized cost of $27000. Exposure is $18000 plus $12000 plus $27000, that is $57000; the returned lease is not counted. Against a hypothetical cap of $60000 the lease may be funded; against a hypothetical cap of $50000 it is not funded at all, and no smaller approval is offered.
